title: Gas and star formation from HD and dust emission in a strongly lensed galaxy
question: Can HD(1-0) emission in the lensed z=5.656 galaxy SPT 0346-52 be used as a molecular gas tracer, and how do HD and dust-SED based gas masses constrain alpha_CO and the starburst nature of the source?

data.angular_resolution: 0.19'' x 0.17'' at PA 57 deg (final continuum-subtracted cube)
data.sensitivity: 0.25 mJy/beam per 15.625 MHz channel (cube); 0.11 mJy/beam (continuum image)

what.value: Lensing magnification mu=5.6 applied to all flux densities

evidence.quote: Each observed flux density was corrected for magnification by assuming a constant lensing magnification of $\mu=5.6$, based on the detailed modelling of $\lambda_{obs}=870\,\mu$m continuum emission (cite: spil16).

what.value: Source radius R_gal ~0.76 kpc from averaged source-plane effective radii

evidence.quote: we average the source-plane $\lambda_{\rm obs}=$2.0 mm and 3.0 mm effective radii of (cite: apos19), resulting in $R_{gal}\sim0.76$ kpc.

what.value: Dust absorption coefficient kappa_o = 0.04 m^2 kg^-1 at 250 GHz

evidence.quote: we assume the dust absorption coefficient $\kappa_o=0.04$ m$^2$ kg$^{-1}$ at $\nu_o=250$ GHz (cite: beel06).

what.value: CO FWHM = 613+/-30 km/s used to set line-free channel exclusion and the assumed HD line width

evidence.quote: based on FWHM$_{\rm CO}=613\pm30$ km s$^{-1}$ (cite: arav16)

what.value: Archival/published continuum flux densities used in the SED (Table 1 entries 1,3-11, 12; ALMA archive projects 2015.1.01580.S, 2013.1.01231.S, 2016.1.00654.S)

evidence.quote: Includes previously published values, values from the ALMA archive, and new values from this paper.
we use the ALMA-staff calibrated continuum images (i.e., no further calibration has been performed).

external_data.citation: (cite: ma15; spil16; jone19; mars14; apos19; dong19; arav16; ma16) and ALMA archive projects as listed in Table 1

what.value: Gas temperature T~60 K from CO LVG modelling, used for f_u in the HD mass

evidence.quote: We assume a gas temperature of $T\sim60$ K, based on Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) modelling of CO(8-7) and CO(2-1) data (cite: dong19).
We also adopt the primordial value of D/H=$(2.6\pm0.1)\times10^{-5}$ ((cite: coc04; plan16; novo17))
we assume that (HD/H$_2$)/(D/H)=1, based on observations of $z\sim2.5$ galaxies with high metallicity and HI column density (cite: lisz15).

what.value: L'CO(2-1)/L'CO(1-0)=0.85 and CO(2-1) flux of earlier work used for alpha_CO

evidence.quote: We convert the CO(2-1) integrated flux density of (cite: arav16) to a CO(1-0) luminosity using $L'_{CO(2-1)}/L'_{CO(1-0)}=0.85$ (appropriate for starburst galaxies) from table 2 of (cite: cari13)

recipe.goal: Image continuum and measure flux density
recipe.method: TCLEAN continuum image from line-free channels (natural weighting, MFS, 3 sigma threshold); total flux integrated inside the 2 sigma contour; 2D Gaussian fits to the three components
key_parameters: natural weighting, multi-frequency synthesis, 3 sigma clean threshold

recipe.method: Tested UVCONTSUB (1st-order, visibilities) and IMCONTSUB on both sidebands; adopted 1st-order IMCONTSUB on the upper sideband excluding +/-250 km/s around HD(1-0)
key_parameters: Initial conservative line exclusion: HD frequency +/-750 km/s (400.888-402.899 GHz) based on CO FWHM
assumptions: HD line width unknown, so conservative channel exclusion used

recipe.goal: Search for HD(1-0) and derive an upper limit on its flux
recipe.method: Channel-by-channel cube search, immoments collapse over -350 to 350 km/s, and spectrum extraction from the 2 sigma continuum mask; undetected, so a 2 sigma upper limit from a Gaussian of FWHM 613 km/s on the RMS at the expected frequency
key_parameters: RMS ~2.15 mJy at the expected frequency; amplitude limit 2 sigma; FWHM 613 km/s
assumptions: HD emission has the same spatial distribution as the FIR continuum and the CO line width

recipe.goal: Fit the dust SED with a modified blackbody
recipe.method: Single-temperature optically-thick modified blackbody with CMB correction, fit to magnification-corrected flux densities (Herschel 24-75 um rest through ALMA/ACT/SPT to rest 451 um; 8 mm point excluded) with 3 free parameters
key_parameters: kappa_o = 0.04 m^2 kg^-1 at 250 GHz; R_gal ~0.76 kpc; mu = 5.6; T_o = 2.73 K
assumptions: Constant magnification mu=5.6, circular source of constant radius, luminosity-weighted single dust temperature, no MIR power law, synchrotron or free-free

recipe.goal: Derive FIR luminosity and star formation rate
recipe.method: Integrate the best-fit model over 42.5-122.5 um and convert with the Kennicutt (1998) scaling

recipe.goal: HD-based molecular gas mass and alpha_CO limit
recipe.method: Convert the HD(1-0) flux limit to M_H2 using N_HD, A10, f_u(T) and primordial D/H; divide by L'CO(1-0) derived from the literature CO(2-1) flux to get alpha_CO
assumptions: (HD/H2)/(D/H)=1; near-primordial D/H at z=5.656; HD kinetic temperature equals CO temperature; only H2 mass (no He or heavy elements)

recipe.method: Gas-to-dust ratio applied to the fitted dust mass (sub-solar metallicity limit) and the Scoville et al. (2016) long-wavelength estimator applied to four flux densities; alpha_CO from each M_H2
key_parameters: Scoville estimator applied to the four points with lambda_rest>250 um (lambda_obs>1664 um); GDR = 100 x 10^(Z-Zsun)
assumptions: Sub-solar metallicity assumed (no metallicity information); Scoville calibration derived from high-metallicity z~0-3 galaxies

answer_key.quantity: Total continuum flux density (rest ~114 um, Band 8)

evidence.quote: The total continuum flux density is $171.5\pm1.0$ mJy.
The continuum is well detected, with a maximum significance of $\sim185\sigma$.

answer_key.quantity: Sum of integrated flux densities of the three Gaussian components

evidence.quote: This value is greater than the sum of each integrated flux density ($147\pm5$ mJy)
resulting in a conservative upper limit on the integrated intensity of HD(1-0) of $F_L<3.8\times10^{-20}$ W m$^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: RMS noise at the expected HD(1-0) frequency in the extracted spectrum

evidence.quote: finding an RMS noise level of $\sim2.15$ mJy at the expected frequency.

answer_key.quantity: Molecular gas mass from HD(1-0) (T~60 K), upper limit

evidence.quote: While no HD(1-0) emission is detected, we are able to place an upper limit on the gas mass of $\rm M_{H_2}<6.4\times10^{11}\,M_{\odot}$.
This results in a limit of $\alpha_{CO}<5.8$.

answer_key.quantity: HD gas-mass limit if Tgas = Tdust = 78.6 K

evidence.quote: resulting in a slightly less conservative upper limit on the gas mass: $\rm M_{H_2}<4.4\times10^{11}\,M_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: HD gas-mass limit if Tgas = 25 K (mass-weighted dust temperature)

evidence.quote: then we find a more conservative gas mass limit of $\rm M_{H_2}<9.9\times10^{12}\,M_{\odot}$.
Fitting a modified blackbody model to our combined dataset yields best-fit values of T$_d=78.6\pm0.5$ K, $\beta=1.81\pm0.03$, and log($M_{dust}/M_{\odot})=8.92\pm0.02$.

Fitting a modified blackbody model to our combined dataset yields best-fit values of T$_d=78.6\pm0.5$ K, $\beta=1.81\pm0.03$, and log($M_{dust}/M_{\odot})=8.92\pm0.02$.
This model exhibits a FIR luminosity (i.e., 42.5-122.5 $\mu$m) of L$_{\rm FIR}=(2.2\pm0.1)\times10^{13}\,$L$_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: Optical depth range across the SED
answer_key.value: 0.22 at lambda_obs=3.0 mm to 43.99 at lambda_obs=160 um; tau~1 at ~200 um

evidence.quote: We find that $\tau_{\nu}$ ranges from the marginally optically thin regime (0.22 at $\lambda_{obs}=3.0$ mm) to optically thick (43.99 at $\lambda_{obs}=160$ $\mu$m)

answer_key.quantity: Gas mass from gas-to-dust ratio (sub-solar metallicity), upper limit

evidence.quote: Since no metallicity information is available, we assume sub-solar metallicity for this early galaxy, resulting in M$_{H_2,GDR}<2.4\times10^{11}$ M$_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: Gas mass from Scoville et al. 2016 estimator

evidence.quote: this yields a magnification-corrected average value of $M_{H_2}=(5.1\pm0.3)\times10^{11}$ M$_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: alpha_CO from GDR and Scoville methods

evidence.quote: resulting in $<5.8$, $<2.2$, and $4.0\pm0.4$ for the HD, GDR, and (cite: scov16) approaches, respectively.
